Filed misogynous-archetypic-nematode for the operator: the rotated-out key 61689bf468f5 is still unrevoked. Not applied.

**Blocker on implementing option (1): the trust config cannot express "the environment the event was written from".** Every class-A event carries `env_id` eea68b7f-…, which is the MCP tracker clone's `.env-id`. The keys are pinned under op-cert env 9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65 (`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID`). Nothing in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` or in the events links the two ids, and ledger entries carry no env_id at all; it is only on the retired raw file. An environment-bound check therefore needs one of these, which is a signing-policy choice:
(a) Accept any pinned environment key, era-scoped, as a signer for any identity, with no writer binding. This needs no config change. It means anyone holding a pinned op-cert key can author as any identity.
(b) Add a per-environment list of writer `.env-id`s to `trusted_environments.yaml` (for 9f1c8e42: eea68b7f). This binds the key to the box's writes. It adds a field to the trust config (Gerrit-gated, CODEOWNERS-protected), and ledger entries would read env_id from their retired raw file.
Class B (the checker misclassifying 906 null-signer entries that verify) does not depend on this choice. Holding implementation until the binding is chosen.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Operator decision (2026-11-19 PST), replacing the earlier option (1) "trust registered env keys from their registration point":

Principle: identity, authorization and op-cert certification are separate concepts. Anyone can sign a plan review, code review or completion verification. Signing is not gated on an allowed identity, and identity can be verified separately when needed.

Decision: `verify-identity` reports a signature that is cryptographically valid, binds its event, and whose key is not on the claimed author's keyring as a separate identity finding, not as `bad-signature`. That finding does not fail the enforced check. The signature check passes when the signature is cryptographically sound and binds the event, and it names the signing key. The bedbug publication hold is measured on the signature check.

Fixed under this ticket as well: the 906 ledger entries with a null signer (class B) are verified instead of being rejected before the check. The 874 unsigned events are out of scope for this decision.

No keyring, trust-file or deployment change follows from this decision. `trusted_environments.yaml` gets no new field, and no key is added to identity 594c's keyring.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Enforced `verify-identity --all` (no `enforce_since`) exits 1 on the tickets history with 7,007 `bad-signature` verdicts, blocking the publication hold of epic polite-antivirus-bedbug. The 2026-11-18 comments establish two classes, each with intact UUID and content-hash binding:
- Class A: 5,858 unique events (1,236 live + 4,622 ledger) signed by the MCP box's op-cert keys under principal 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d. Neither key is on 594c's keyring, so `verify_authorship_any_key` fails and `_verify_signed` returns `bad-signature`.
- Class B: 906 unique ledger entries signed by keys that ARE on 594c's keyring, but compaction recorded `signer_pubkey: null`. `_verify_signed` rejects them before any verify.

Operator decision (2026-11-19, revised after code review): a cryptographically valid, event-binding signature whose key is not on the claimed author's keyring gets its own verdict, `signer-not-on-keyring`, distinct from `bad-signature`, and FAILS the enforced check like `key_not_valid_at_era` (advisory mode only reports it); the output names the signing key. Class B is verified. The 874 unsigned events are out of scope. No keyring, trust-file, deployment, config-key, env-var or flag change.

## Approach
Change only the classifier and its report, in `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`:
1. Delete the null-`signer_pubkey` short-circuit in `_verify_signed`, so a null-signer ledger entry runs the same era and any-key verify as every other entry. Compaction keeps recording `signer_pubkey` (`compact_txn.py` unchanged); only this check stops reading it. `_verify_signed`'s complexity drops from its baseline 16 to 15, a stale entry the ratchet accepts (baseline file not edited).
2. Add a sixth verdict `signer-not-on-keyring` (constant `SIGNER_NOT_ON_KEYRING`). When the any-key verify fails, `_verify_signed` runs one more verify through a new helper `_verifies_against_own_key(envelope, author_id)`: it reads the signer's public key out of the SSHSIG blob with the existing `sshsig.embedded_public_key` (`src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py`), builds a one-key trust root with `authorship.allowed_signers_from_keys`, and calls `registry.verify(authorship.AUTHORSHIP_KIND, ...)`, which is the same `ssh-keygen -Y verify` path (signature, namespace and principal all checked; never `check-novalidate`). Verified there means `signer-not-on-keyring`; otherwise `bad-signature`. The subject UUID/content-hash binding check already runs earlier in `_verify_signed` and still returns `bad-signature` on mismatch, so a non-binding or tampered signature keeps failing.
3. `cli` counts the new verdict, prints it in the summary line after `key-not-valid-at-era`, lists it as a problem line, and counts it in `enforced_not_verified` like every other non-verified verdict. Every listed signed problem line and every JSON report entry names the signing key as its OpenSSH `SHA256:` fingerprint, computed with the existing `signer_key_id` in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py` (null for unsigned or unparseable signatures). The JSON entry's `display` for the new verdict is `unverified`. Report-line building moves into a small helper so `cli` stays under its complexity ceiling. ADR 0045 gains an amendment and the verify-identity help text names the verdict.
4. `src/rebar/schemas/verify_identity_report.schema.json` gains a required `signing_key` property (string or null) and documents the new verdict.
5. `src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_dry_run.py` parses the extended summary line (`_COUNT_RE` and `_COUNT_KEYS` gain `signer_not_on_keyring`).

This fits because it is a classification change inside one verifier reusing `sshsig.embedded_public_key`; no new trust source or mechanism. Checked in-session: null-signer ledger entries for 4 distinct keys verify `certified` against their embedded key; a tampered payload returns `mismatch`.

Portability: verification logic only; no new subprocess, fd, path, encoding or permission handling. No Windows sweep.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py (classifier, summary, report, helpers)
- src/rebar/schemas/verify_identity_report.schema.json (signing_key, verdict docs)
- src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_dry_run.py (summary-line parser)
- tests/unit/test_identity_ts3_117b.py (replace the two Mallory "forged" tests, whose case is now the identity finding; add class-B and genuinely-bad cases)
- tests/unit/test_identity_ac7_bff8.py (JSON entry carries signing_key)
- tests/unit/test_reclaim_dry_run.py (parsed counts include the new key)
- docs/identity.md, docs/identity-setup.md (verdict vocabulary)

## Testing
Tests first (RED against origin/main), in `tests/unit/test_identity_ts3_117b.py`:
- Off-keyring, live: Ada's event signed by Mallory's key (Statement binds the event). Enforced `verify-identity --all` exits 1 and prints `signer-not-on-keyring` with Mallory's `SHA256:` fingerprint (`ssh-keygen -lf`); advisory mode exits 0.
- Off-keyring, compacted: the same event after `rebar.compact` (ledger `signer_pubkey` is null) gives the same verdict and exit 1.
- Null-signer ledger entry with a genuinely bad signature: `bad-signature`, exit 1.
- Class B: a keyring-signed event compacted, its ledger `signer_pubkey` set to null and committed; enforced run exits 0 with 0 bad-signature.
- Genuinely bad signature: an envelope whose payload binds the event but whose signature bytes come from signing a different event's Statement with Mallory's key gives `bad-signature` and exit 1.
- Non-binding: a Mallory-signed Statement for event X attached to event Y gives `bad-signature` and exit 1.
- JSON: `--format json` on the off-keyring store emits an entry with `verdict` `signer-not-on-keyring`, `display` `unverified`, `signing_key` equal to the fingerprint, validating against the schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A cryptographically valid, event-binding signature by a key not on the author's keyring is classified `signer-not-on-keyring` (not `bad-signature`) and names its `SHA256:` signing key, for live and compacted events; verified by the off-keyring tests in `tests/unit/test_identity_ts3_117b.py`.
- [ ] `signer-not-on-keyring` fails the enforced check (exit 1) and is only reported in advisory mode (exit 0); verified by `test_off_keyring_signature_fails_enforcement` and `test_off_keyring_signature_passes_in_advisory_mode`.
- [ ] A null-`signer_pubkey` ledger entry signed by a keyring key classifies `verified`; verified by the class-B test.
- [ ] A signature that fails cryptographic verification, or does not bind its event, still classifies `bad-signature` and exits 1, including a null-signer ledger entry; verified by the three bad-signature tests.
- [ ] The JSON report entry carries `signing_key` and validates against `verify_identity_report.schema.json`; verified by `tests/unit/test_identity_ac7_bff8.py::test_json_report_shape_and_schema` and the new JSON test.
- [ ] `reclaim_dry_run` parses the extended summary line; verified by `tests/unit/test_reclaim_dry_run.py::test_dry_run_writes_a_passing_evidence_packet` asserting the `signer_not_on_keyring` count.
- [ ] `make verify` passes in the worktree, and the change merges through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Enforced `verify-identity --all` run with the merged build on a no-remote clone of the original tickets history reports 0 bad-signature, 0 unknown-author and 0 key-not-valid-at-era; the per-verdict counts are recorded as a comment on this ticket and on polite-antivirus-bedbug.
  provenance: environment=operator Mac with local no-remote copies of the tickets history; principal=agent session 3d705fec; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — `python -m rebar verify-identity --all` from a worktree at merged origin/main reads histories outside the repository, so the counts are attested in ticket comments; nothing is pushed or published.
